589.title: fix(checkpoint): resolve HF repo Ids before conversion
589.reason: Goal is right, but resolving at the CLI with download_hf_weight only fetches weight shards, so a fresh HF cache still lacks tokenizer/remote-code files and the API path (convert_checkpoint) stays unfixed. Own version resolves inside convert_checkpoint, pulls the metadata too, and adds tests.

591.title: perf(moe): fold the shared-expert gate epilogue into hc_combine_norm
591.reason: Stacked on #590; adopted together as one own implementation. Folding the shared-expert epilogue is right, but the PR dispatches on an isinstance tuple and returns an un-combined 3-tuple from each layer; own version passes shared/gate explicitly and links each layer to its consumer norm (link_next_norms).

590.title: perf(model): fuse hc combine with the next block's RMSNorm via hc_combine_norm
590.reason: Goal is worthwhile (one launch fewer per block). The PR gets bit-exactness by reshaping to match the standalone norm's reduction tree; own version makes both kernels call one _gemma_rmsnorm helper on the same flat tile with the same num_warps, so they match by construction, and adds CPU and whole-stack fused==split tests.

587.title: feat(rocm): run on RDNA3/RDNA4 with torch 2.14/2.15 and ROCm 7.14/10
587.reason: ROCm support is worthwhile, but the PR widens torch to <2.16 and triton to <3.9 and switches to C++20 for CUDA users too (sglang-kernel links only against 2.11), and on ROCm 7.14 it keeps a hiprtc-compiled spin kernel busy on a CU. Own version leaves the CUDA pins alone (uv overrides script for ROCm), uses C++20 only for ROCm torch>=2.14, detects memop graph replay functionally and falls back to the host-callback sync, and adds a moe_align contract test that runs on CPU. ROCm is untested here.

585.title: perf(linear): run a single-row bf16 projection as one GEMV
585.reason: Worthwhile decode bs=1 bandwidth win. The PR turns on the GEMV for every bf16 linear, including ROCm and narrow layers, has no width heuristic, and leaves the tied LM head on F.linear. Own version gates on NVIDIA and >=512 out features, makes it opt-out with linear.none=torch, requires a row-major weight, uses ValueError checks, and covers the tied head.

578.title: perf(moe): dequant nvfp4 prefill experts by bit placement and load activations contiguously
578.reason: Bit-identical output, ~6x faster NVFP4 MoE prefill GEMM (measured by the author), reusing nvfp4_linear's existing table-free decode; the exactness argument checks out (every e2m1*e4m3 product is exact in fp16/bf16). Nothing to improve.

575.title: fix(windows): build the extensions and JIT kernels with MSVC
575.reason: Windows source build. On Linux it only respells (.template, __forceinline__) to byte-identical device code; the rest sits behind sys.platform. Likely supersedes the older Windows PRs #298/#285 (to check when reached). setup.py conflict with our ROCm change resolved in the merge commit.

574.title: feat(engine): --vram-reserve-mb keeps VRAM free at the largest prefill
574.reason: Opt-in (--vram-reserve-mb, default 0) measurement of the real prefill peak with a bounded shrink of the expert cache; inert otherwise, tested. Draft #583 (WDDM free memory) builds on it.

572.title: fix(server): keep a silent stream alive and notice a client that left
572.reason: Small and well tested: SSE comment keep-alive while a long prefill is silent, plus disconnect detection during the silence. Complements, not duplicates, #222 (abort delivery), which is still to be reviewed.

577.title: feat(kvcache): keep prefill-chunk GDN checkpoints in a pinned host bank
577.reason: Compared with an independent implementation of the same goal (+349 vs +636 lines, same design: pinned host bank, device copy wins, LRU host eviction, exact-length attach, plus the same last_track_seqlen carry fix). Ours was smaller but only CPU-tested; the PR is validated on a live engine and already fixed an overlap-scheduling bug found there, which weighs more for pinned-memory/stream-ordering code. Opt-in (--mamba-host-slots, default 0). Includes #505's fix, so #505 is likely superseded; #525 is a broader alternative to check when reached.

505.title: fix(scheduler): preserve pending hybrid checkpoint across prefill chunks
505.reason: Its fix (carry mamba_last_track_seqlen into the next chunk's Req, three lines in scheduler/prefill.py) is contained verbatim in #577, which credits it and is already merged.

334.title: fix(memory): honor cgroup memory limits when sizing expert banks
334.reason: Right goal (containers were OOM-killed mid-load because the loader sized against the host's MemAvailable). The PR's 294-line module charges memory.current in full, which counts page cache: a container that just read its checkpoint reads as full. Own ~90-line version clamps MemAvailable to the tightest cgroup v2/v1 limit and counts inactive_file as free; used by the expert-bank loader, ft bench bw and the load bench.

233.title: fix(engine): probe the real WSL pin budget instead of guessing 40% RAM
233.reason: Right goal (WSL refuses pinning far below the 40%-of-RAM guess, so loads died in cudaHostRegister). The PR probes at most 8 GiB (capping large hosts at 6.4 GiB), returns None = uncapped when nothing pins, and predates main's reserved-bytes signature. Own version probes up to the old estimate via the pinned extension (which clears the latched error, #144), returns 0 when nothing pins, and is cached.

144.title: fix(kernel): clear the latched CUDA error before raising in pinned_tensor
144.reason: A refused pin (low RAM) left the CUDA error latched, so the next unrelated CUDA call failed as if it were its own -- it breaks exactly the fallback paths a low-RAM load relies on. Clean, HIP mappings already exist.

56.title: kernel: clamp zero-size host registrations; WDDM lock-pool hint on pin failure
56.reason: The empty-bank failure is real but now hits earlier: an anonymous mmap of 0 bytes raises EINVAL before host_register, so the PR's clamp no longer helps. Own fix gives an empty bank one block, an empty tensor and device_ptr()=0. The PR's RLIMIT_MEMLOCK hint is dropped (cudaHostRegister is not bound by it); main already has PinFailed + _pin_hint.

337.title: feat(moe): NVMe disk tier for MoE expert banks
337.reason: Pulled forward (low-RAM topic): lets models whose expert banks exceed host RAM run, the tail served from NVMe. Opt-in (--moe-disk-tier); the one general change, MAP_PRIVATE banks, makes released pages really free. Fixups: Windows mmap has no flags (would break every bank on Windows), pin_prefix of an empty bank pinned 0 bytes, and a family test stale against main's dialect-dependent qwen3_5_moe spec. Conflicts with #563 in 6 files; the user chose #337.

563.title: feat(moe): pin hot experts so fp8 qwen3.8-flash-next serves on a 48gb card
563.reason: Valuable idea (pin per-layer hot experts in VRAM, hotness stats + selection tool, EMA repinning, live K via tune file, fp8_block CPU executor from #534), but 9.4k lines incl. a 1.2k-line rewrite of the offload cache, measured on one machine, and not opt-in: it changes the hybrid PCIe/CPU split default from the benched profile to a fixed 50%. Conflicts with the adopted #337 in 6 files. User decision: come back after all other PRs, then likely build our own version -- with a GPU test environment.

564.title: fix(server): do not auto-select qwen3 parser for instruct-2507
564.reason: Small, tested: --reasoning-parser auto no longer picks qwen3 for Instruct-2507 checkpoints (empty message.content). The model path is the only signal (shared architecture with Thinking-2507); acceptable for an auto heuristic, an explicit flag still wins.

562.title: fix(engine): charge the attention workspace in moe-cache-auto sizing
562.reason: Charges the attention backend's fixed workspace (fi 256 MiB, trtllm 128 MiB) in the --moe-cache-auto plan, so a tight --memory-ratio no longer OOMs at startup. Fixup: the runtime rebuild fit check (validate_rebuild, generic + DSV4) did not charge it, so a rebuild could re-grant the bytes the workspace holds. #340 (dummy page in the KV floor) is a separate, complementary fix.

559.title: fix(kvcache): clone inserted radix keys to release request buffers
559.reason: Correct and small: radix keys were views into the request's whole input+output token buffer, so a cached 16-token prefix kept ~131 KB alive (host-RAM growth). Fixup: the regression test the PR left out, across plain/SWA/hybrid caches.

305.title: feat(server): add --api-key bearer authentication
305.reason: Pulled forward while reviewing #558 (same feature). The more complete --api-key: tests, docs, WWW-Authenticate, CORS preflight passes, and the attached shell client carries the key (with #558 a keyed ft serve --shell would lock out its own shell). args.py conflict resolved in the merge commit.

558.title: feat(server): --api-key flag for bearer token auth on the HTTP API
558.reason: Same --api-key feature as #305, which is more complete (tests, docs, CORS preflight, WWW-Authenticate, the shell client sends the key) and is merged.

565.title: fix(ple): strict shard schema/geometry, nofollow + bounded discovery, mutation evidence, and pinned-bank admission/rollback
565.reason: Two of its four parts are worth having: one shard-set schema/geometry check shared by both PLE backends (exact row count, errors naming tensor+file), and pinned admission against available host RAM with release on failure (low-RAM topic). Own version (+396/-140 vs +981/-107) builds on available_host_memory() from #334's reimplementation and leaves out nofollow discovery and per-shard identity/digest re-validation -- tamper hardening a local engine does not need.

593.title: fix(checkpoint): refuse converting into a directory that already holds an FTW
593.reason: Real data-loss bug: --out pointing at an existing FTW dir overwrote shard 00000 under a stale index. Merged as is (conflict with main's _resolve_source, kept both); fixup moves the check ahead of _resolve_source so an hf repo id is not downloaded only to be refused, with a test that fails before.

592.title: fix(mm): classify image fetch errors and re-check redirect targets
592.reason: Redirects were followed without re-checking --allowed-media-domains (the code even said so), so an allowed host could 302 into the operator's network; 400 bodies leaked local paths and errno text. Small, tested, also streams with the size cap instead of buffering. Merged unchanged.

553.title: feat(server): publish cumulative prefill and decode timing on /v1/stats
553.reason: Cumulative counters let a poller diff two /v1/stats calls into prefill/decode tok/s; per-request state follows the same finished-reply lifecycle as _inflight, so no new leak. Overlaps #447 only on a cached-tokens counter. Merged unchanged.

551.title: improve installation success rate with higher timeout and retries
551.reason: Longer uv HTTP timeout/retries fix real installer timeouts on slow links to pypi.nvidia.com. Fixup makes them defaults (${UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT:-600}) so a user-set value still wins.

535.title: ci(rocm): add ROCm 10.0.0 Dockerfile and validation workflow
535.reason: CI for upstream's self-hosted W7900D runner (custom labels); this fork has no such runner, and a full run needs ROCm support PRs not yet adopted. Not wrong, just not runnable here yet: revisit together with the ROCm backend PR #217.

531.title: fix(server): clamp /v1/models context_length to the allocated KV pool
531.reason: /v1/models advertised the model ceiling while the engine admits against min(ceiling, num_pages*page_size), so `ft launch` sized agent windows past the KV pool. Fixup: multiply only by the engine-reported page_size (the frontend's config.page_size is unresolved), with a test. Live on Qwen3-0.6B (RTX 4090): /v1/models reports the 3000-page pool once the engine meta lands.

527.title: fix(sampling): apply presence and frequency penalties
527.reason: The API accepted presence/frequency penalties but ignored them. PR keeps a vocab-sized count tensor per request and ships no tests; ours rebuilds counts each step from the generated tokens in token_pool on the engine stream (overlap-safe, no state across aborts or table reuse), enforces OpenAI's [-2, 2] with a 400, adds CPU and GPU tests (mixed batch passed on the RTX 4090). Live on Qwen3-0.6B under overlap scheduling: an in-process spy over 636 penalty steps found the counted tokens always equal the request's real output prefix; 400 on out-of-range values.

525.title: feat(kvcache): host-resident prefix tier for hybrid GDN models (snapshots + KV pages)
525.reason: Stacked on the still-undecided #499 (KV host-offload, its commits are in this diff); 1.5k lines, opt-in via env flags. Review together with #499 once the queue reaches it. 2026-10-03: #499 deferred until after the queue, so this follows it.

507.title: feat(glm5_next): serve GLM-5.3-Flash with tensor parallelism
507.reason: TP for glm5_next (MLA/DSA heads, KDA heads, MLPs, NVFP4 experts sharded on I); TP=1 paths unchanged, author ran it on 4x A4000. Fixup: the TP test fixture lacked num_key_value_heads, which transformers 5.16 validates. Single-GPU tests pass; TP itself untested here (one GPU).

504.title: feat(server): serve per-request inference metrics under --enable-metrics-report
504.reason: Opt-in per-request TTFT/prefill/decode metrics on chat, messages and responses; complements the cumulative /v1/stats counters from #553. Fixup: the abort test stub (newer than the PR's base) needed the new _prefill_start map. Live on Qwen3-0.6B: metrics object served with plausible TTFT/prefill/decode values.

354.title: feat(kvcache): store the KV cache as fp8 e4m3 codes (--kv-cache-dtype fp8)
354.reason: Best of the KV-quant group: e4m3 codes + one fp32 scale per (token, kv head), robust to outliers; covers MHA (incl. GDN hybrid), hybrid-SWA, QSA and MLA/DSA. On the 27B = RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 on the RTX 4090, --max-running-requests 1 --memory-ratio 0.95 --max-prefill-length 2048: KV 13420 -> 26427 tokens, decode 46.2 vs 46.6 tok/s (triton instead of fi), same quality (Q&A, 8k fact retrieval, 15 codes in 7.4k); coherent on Qwen3-0.6B where #126 produced NaN. Fixups: test doubles for newer main attributes, one-bf16-ulp tolerance for an sm_89 summation-order case, help/docs now say MLA/DSA is covered.

408.title: feat(kvcache): add nvfp4 kv quantization
408.reason: nvfp4 KV on top of #354 (software decode on sm_89): 3.46x the bf16 tokens (46476 on the 27B) with the same quality on both models; costs ~15% decode at 8k and ~10% prefill, so it is opt-in. Fixup: kv_row_bytes sizes the packed row instead of kv_storage_bytes_per_elem raising 'unknown kv_quant'.

309.title: feat(kvcache): add reliable quantized KV cache
309.reason: fp8_e4m3 crashes at CUDA-graph capture (a triton.jit kernel imports round_e4m3; its tests never run that kernel), needs an explicit --attention-backend triton, q4_0 degrades badly on Qwen3-0.6B, q6_0 is 25% slower at 8k decode. fp8 and the sub-byte budget are covered by #354 + #408.

268.title: feat(kvcache): sub-byte Q4_0 and Q6_0 KV cache quantization
268.reason: Earlier version of #309's sub-byte work (same jit-import bug) plus unrelated Windows/csrc changes; covered by #354 + #408.

126.title: Add fp8 KV-cache quantization (--kv-dtype)
126.reason: Fixed scale 1.0 ignores checkpoint k/v scales: K values of 488 exceed e4m3's 448 and the cast yields NaN (garbage on Qwen3-0.6B); MHA + fi only, no tests. An fi fp8 path could return later on top of #354 with proper scales.

398.title: feat(kvcache): add ISO3/ISO4 KV-cache quantization (--kv-cache-iso)
398.reason: ISO3/ISO4 produce garbage on Qwen3-0.6B, 8k decode drops to 6-9 tok/s (about 7x slower), FULL attention only, forces its own backend and adds ~1k lines of custom CUDA.

498.title: feat(qwen4_exp): support channel-wise fp8 dense weights and per-row PLE loaders
498.reason: Special-case loader support for community per_row_e4m3 PLE exports and channel-wise fp8 dense weights (extra kernel branch + loader paths for one non-standard checkpoint dialect); conflicts with the PLE/dense loading reworked by #594. Not worth carrying.

500.title: perf(moe): single-launch prefill buffer invalidation without hidden sync
500.reason: Replaces the per-buffer prefill invalidation with a single launch and drops a hidden host sync; adds offload tests. Fixup: trimmed the long invalidation comments to the repo's comment style. tests/moe/test_offload.py passes on the RTX 4090.

594.title: feat(qwen4_exp): support ModelOpt QAD checkpoints (NVFP4 PLE tables, MXFP8 dense)
594.reason: Loads ModelOpt QAD checkpoints: NVFP4-packed PLE tables and MXFP8 dense scales under .weight_scale. Merge conflict resolved by routing the NVFP4 table through main's validating scan_ple_table and host-RAM admission check. Fixup: the scan checks the row count against the n-gram config, and the cuda gather oob test indexes per row. qwen4_exp tests pass on the RTX 4090 (3 test_qsa_backend chunked-prefill failures predate the merge); the NVFP4 gather path itself is not exercised end to end on sm_89.

495.title: fix(scheduler): wait for rank subscribers before first broadcast
495.reason: Real ZMQ slow-joiner race: with tp>1, rank 0 could broadcast before a rank's SUB subscription reached the PUB, dropping the message and hanging both ranks. XPUB + wait_for_subscribers closes it; both ranks reach the IO mixin right after engine init, so the 30 s wait cannot deadlock. Small, with a pub/sub test; tests/utils pass. TP>1 itself is not testable on the single 4090.

499.title: feat(kvcache): host-RAM KV tier for sparse-attention models (--kv-host-pages)
499.reason: Its fp8 parts (16-bit indexer dtype guard, k/v scales on the QSA attend) are already on main via #354. The remaining host-RAM KV tier (~700 lines: LRU GPU page cache over a pinned host mirror, per-row prefill attend loop) only serves QSA models (qwen4_exp / Flash-Next), ships without tests, and cannot be run here: only the Flash-Next config is cached and 30 GB RAM cannot hold its weights. Interesting for long context; revisit after the queue together with #525 and the CPU-embedding work.

502.title: feat(deepseek_v4): serve image input on the V4-Flash-Vision release
502.reason: 1.3k-line vision path for DeepSeek-V4-Flash. Not judged on its merits yet: the model is far beyond a single RTX 4090 with 30 GB RAM, so it cannot be run or verified here; it also reworks the shared mm pad scheme across every processor and the scheduler's mm spans, which needs a careful review. Revisit after the queue (or when it lands upstream).

494.title: fix(gemma4): load mixed-quant GGUF checkpoints
494.reason: Mixed-quant Gemma4 GGUFs (per-tensor quant types inside one expert bank) failed to load; the PR dequantizes or repacks the odd tensors and passes each expert's byte stride to ggml_moe_a8_vec. Comes with tests. GPU-checked on the RTX 4090: a q8_0 bank with padded expert stride gave NaN before and now matches the contiguous bank bit for bit and a dequantized reference (rel. err 0.6%). No Gemma4 GGUF is cached, so no end-to-end load.

493.title: fix(gemma4): load mixed compressed-tensors nvfp4
493.reason: Gemma4 compressed-tensors checkpoints that mix nvfp4 and unquantized tensors failed to load; nvfp4_expert_spec now follows the installed QuantConfig's dialect. Fixup: tests/moe/test_disk_tier_families excludes gemma4 from the static-spec check, as for qwen3_5_moe. CPU tests pass; the nvfp4 compute path needs FP4 hardware that sm_89 lacks, but the change is load-side only.

488.title: fix(swa): keep the prompt head's windowed KV so fan-out can reuse a shared prefix
488.reason: With sliding-window attention the radix cache dropped the windowed KV of a shared prompt head, so fan-out (n>1, parallel requests on one prefix) re-prefilled it. Small change in scheduler/cache.py with retention and stress tests; tests/scheduler pass on the RTX 4090 machine. Later fixup (6f18f27): its stress test set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' at import, hiding the GPU from every other test in the same pytest session (130 'Invalid device id' failures); it now patches _maybe_pinned locally instead.

487.title: fix(server): hoist system messages to front for templates requiring system-first
487.reason: Qwen3.6+ templates (Qwen3.8-27B included) raise 'System message must be at the beginning.' on a later system message. The PR hoisted and merged system messages in render_messages for every model, reordering prompts for templates that render them in place (Qwen3). Ours renders as sent and only on a TemplateError retries with the system messages merged at the front; unrelated template errors re-raise. Checked on the cached Qwen3-0.6B (unchanged) and Qwen3.8-27B (now renders) templates.

484.title: feat(scheduler): interleave decode steps into long prefill runs
484.reason: Opt-in --decode-interleave-every N: after N consecutive prefill chunks one decode step runs, so a long chunked prefill no longer stalls in-flight decodes. Unset keeps the old order; tests drive the real _schedule_next_batch. Live on the RTX 4090 (Qwen3-0.6B, 256-token chunks, ~20k-token prompt while a stream decodes): longest decode gap 525 ms -> 44 ms (N=4) / 23 ms (N=1); decode tokens during the prefill 12 -> 32 / 85; prefill 0.60 s -> 0.61 s / 0.70 s.

477.title: feat(server): expose POST /v1/tokenize endpoint for client-side token counting
477.reason: Useful llama.cpp-style token counting endpoint (auth comes from the --api-key middleware). Fixup: the messages path ignored tools, chat_template_kwargs, reasoning_effort and the server's thinking default, so it undercounted against usage.prompt_tokens; it now converts the body through chat_request_to_genspec, and an invalid body is a 400. Merge conflict on the generation imports (build_metrics from #504) resolved by keeping both.

476.title: feat(server): add --default-thinking-mode flag for server-wide thinking default
476.reason: Server-wide thinking default for clients that never send chat_template_kwargs. Fixup: the PR injected the default before effort_toggle_kwargs, which keeps an existing thinking key, so under --default-thinking-mode chat a request's reasoning_effort / thinking.type / Responses reasoning.effort were silently ignored. The default now applies last, treats every thinking spelling as explicit, broadcasts like the protocol toggles, and also applies to /v1/messages/count_tokens. Regression tests run through the three real request converters.

475.title: fix(tokenizer): respect explicit enable_thinking=false even when tools present
475.reason: resolve_thinking_mode forced thinking whenever tools were offered, overriding an explicit enable_thinking=false / thinking=false. Six lines plus a test; CPU tokenizer tests pass. No GPU relevance.

468.title: fix(engine): reject fa attention backend below sm_90 at config time
468.reason: Claims the fa backend (sgl_kernel flash-attn) cannot run below sm_90 and gates it at config time. Refuted on the RTX 4090 (sm_89) with sgl_kernel 0.4.5: flash_attn_varlen_func matches an SDPA reference (max err 0.009 in bf16) and ft serve --attention-backend fa on Qwen3-0.6B gets through CUDA-graph capture and serves. The gate would block a working backend on Ada; the reported failure likely came from an older sgl_kernel build without sm_89 kernels.

466.title: fix(utils): tolerate coalesced msgpack frames in zmq pull queues
466.reason: Buffers msgpack frames in the zmq pull/sub queues so a frame with two packed objects no longer crashes a worker (seen on Windows). ZMQ delivers whole messages, so such a frame points to a sender-side race the PR would mask instead of fix; a frame holding a partial object still crashes (take() raises IndexError on an empty buffer) and its leftover bytes corrupt the next frame. Windows-only symptom with an unknown root cause; not reproducible here.

464.title: fix(scheduler): match stop strings with incremental decoding
464.reason: The scheduler matched stop strings on a window of max_chars+1 tokens decoded on its own, so a stop over multi-token characters (rare CJK, emoji under byte-level BPE) was missed, a half-decoded character could match, and the detokenizer then failed to trim the stop. Now matches against the same incremental decode the detokenizer streams. The PR had no tests; fixup adds five (four fail before). Live on Qwen3-0.6B: CJK stop strings trim correctly, same as before for single-token characters.

461.title: fix(server): loopback-bind the TP rendezvous store, add --dist-port
461.reason: torch's TCPStore server ignores the host and listens on every interface, so the rendezvous store at --port+1 was reachable off-box without authentication, also with one GPU. Verified here: the old store listened on *:PORT (incl. the LAN address), the PR's pre-bound one on 127.0.0.1 only; live server shows 127.0.0.1:30112. Adds --dist-port. Merge conflict with --api-key in args.py/docs resolved by keeping both. Fixup: Windows keeps the previous store with a warning (master_listen_fd with a SOCKET handle is untested there and SO_REUSEADDR lets another socket take the port).

460.title: feat(models): support deepseek v4.1 with native fp8-fp4 kv storage
460.reason: 15k-line DeepSeek V4.1 port (132 files: new sparse attention, native fp8/fp4 KV storage, checkpoint conversion). Not judged on its merits yet: the model is far beyond a single RTX 4090 with 30 GB RAM, so it cannot be run or verified here, and it touches shared attention/KV code that needs a careful review. Revisit after the queue (or when it lands upstream).

459.title: fix(checkpoint): validate FTW v1 indexes eagerly
459.reason: Validates the FTW index once at open (integer ranges, required fields, duplicate keys, safe shard names, shard coverage/sizes, tensor overlaps) and raises FTWFormatError instead of failing deep in mmap/O_DIRECT; 640 lines of tests. Fixup: it also demanded that tensors cover every byte with no gaps, but scripts/ftw_hotfix.py drops/replaces entries and compacts their shards one atomic index swap at a time, promising a loadable FTW at every step and after an interrupted run; those indexes have unreferenced bytes inside a shard. Gaps are now accepted, overlaps still rejected. On the RTX 4090: a fresh ft checkpoint of Qwen3-0.6B validates (227 tensors) and generates token-identical greedy output to the safetensors path.

456.title: Lowvram 4gb
456.reason: Built on a much older main: it would revert large parts of current code (quant config plumbing, moe_strategy, gpu selection, EngineConfig post-init), defines resolved_kv_dtype twice, adds [WEIGHT-DIAG] debug prints, and ships AI work logs and a PDF under docs/. Its fp8 KV storage is on main via #354. The CPU-resident embedding idea is planned as our own --embed-device cpu after the queue, crediting this PR's author (see deferred CPU-embedding work).

451.title: docs(moe): report shared expert banks across replicas
451.reason: Field report of a two-replica experiment on 2x RTX 5090 that relies on an external shared-bank shim not in the repo; linked from the README it reads like a supported feature. Documents something FreeToken does not contain.

447.title: feat(moe): owner-local expert parallelism and tensor parallelism
447.reason: 5k-line owner-local expert parallelism + TP for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on the offload MoE backend (experts partitioned whole across ranks, one all-reduce per MoE layer, graph-capturable routing). Not judged on its merits yet: needs several GPUs and the Flash-Next weights, neither available here. Revisit after the queue.

440.title: fix(models): build o_proj row-parallel in the remaining column-parallel families
440.reason: gemma4, qwen3_5_moe and muse_glimmer paired a head-sharded qkv with a replicated o_proj, which would be silently wrong under TP>1 (no all-reduce); LinearOProj is the row-parallel layer every other family uses and is identical at TP=1. Checked on the RTX 4090: Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 (qwen3_5 attention) gives token-identical greedy output on three prompts before and after.

439.title: fix(scheduler): read the prefill chunk cap from the pool, not a snapshot
439.reason: CacheManager copied the window pool's prefill_chunk_budget at construction, so a runtime cache rebuild never refreshed it: growing the pool left chunking unchanged, shrinking left a cap too large for the pool. Now a property that re-reads the pool; test drives a real DSV4 pool rebuild in both directions. CPU tests pass; DSV4 itself cannot run here.

435.title: fix(server): resolve JSON Schema refs and union types in tool arguments
435.reason: Resolves local $ref (cycle-safe), type unions and anyOf/oneOf when typing tool-call arguments in the schema-aware parsers (qwen3_coder, MiniMax M3), with 700 lines of tests. Fixup: it gave every property without a type the new 'loose' type, so a parameter declared only by description or enum stopped streaming as a string and '123'/'true' came back as a number/boolean; only unions and unresolvable refs now parse loosely, plain untyped properties keep the string default (new test, 20 cases fail before).

430.title: fix(glm4_moe): load compressed-tensors NVFP4 expert checkpoints
430.reason: glm4_moe's expert reader only knew the modelopt names, so a compressed-tensors export (gesong2077/GLM-4.5-Air-NVFP4) matched only the shared weight_scale tensors and the banks filled with scales and no weights. Mirrors glm5_next's dialect handling (kind_map + reciprocal global scale). The PR had no tests; fixup moves glm4_moe out of the static-spec test (its hook now reads the config) and adds dialect tests. The ~60 GB model cannot run here.

429.title: qwen4_exp: build o_proj row-parallel, as every other family does
429.reason: Same latent TP>1 defect as #440 for qwen4_exp: replicated o_proj after a head-sharded qkv would skip the all-reduce. LinearOProj is identical at TP=1 (#440's 27B check showed token-identical output for the same swap); qwen4_exp CPU tests pass. Flash-Next itself cannot run here.

414.title: fix(kernel): order the batch-memcpy probe against the current stream
414.reason: The cudaMemcpyBatchAsync probe zero-filled its destination on the current stream and copied on a fresh stream without a join, so under a stream backlog the fill clobbered the copy and the probe failed on supported hardware, silently disabling --moe-prefill-hit-d2d. One wait_stream fixes it. Reproduced on the RTX 4090: the PR's test fails without the fix and passes with it.

413.title: fix(models): support llm-compressor NVFP4 MoE export variants
413.reason: Adds detection and loaders for llm-compressor Qwen3.5-MoE NVFP4 export variants (per-expert vs stacked experts, GDN left bf16/fp8, format-only configs, NVFP4 lm_head/embed, single-file checkpoints). Some gaps are still real on main (its tests show format-only configs detected as 'none' and compressed-tensors block-fp8 refused), but the PR predates the QuantConfig refactor (#418/#438) and conflicts in all six code files, so it needs a reimplementation on the new layers, verified against a real export. Revisit together with the MoE test model choice (a Qwen3.5/3.6-MoE NVFP4 export would make it directly testable).

412.title: fix(bench): show how to use custom bandwidth profiles
412.reason: ft bench bw -o <path> wrote a profile that serving never read unless FREETOKEN_BENCHBW_PATH pointed at it; the report now prints that export. bench_profile.py reads exactly that variable. Test passes.

406.title: docs(models): qualify full GLM-5.3 on H200 Serverless
406.reason: Documents full GLM-5.3 on the existing glm_moe_dsa path with a community NVFP4 conversion (LibertAIDAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4), renames the AOT entry to it with the NVIDIA/zai 5.2 names as aliases, adds a config test and ~900 lines of raw H200 benchmark JSON. Not judged on its merits yet: the model cannot run or be verified here. Revisit after the queue.

405.title: fix(models): serve qwen4_exp FTW checkpoints with PLE streamed from source
405.reason: Falls back to the conversion source to stream the Flash-Next PLE table from an FTW dir. Superseded by #420 on main (3d919e9): the converter now writes the PLE table next to the FTW, and scripts/ftw_hotfix.py adds it to FTWs converted before that.

399.title: fix(cpu-moe): honor padded fp8 scale strides, add avx512f tier and float64 parity (builds on #36)
399.reason: Reviewed together with #36, whose block-FP8 CPU GEMV (W8A16 for --moe-strategy cpu/hybrid; FP8 checkpoints had no CPU expert path) it contains. On top: the scale banks are padded per expert to 16 bytes (Qwen3.x down_scale 5 -> 6 cols), which #36 alone mis-strides; an avx512f tier for CPUs without avx512_bf16; float64 parity tests that force each ISA tier. On this VM (AVX2 only; the two AVX-512 tiers skip): 11 tests pass; ft bench bw now measures fp8 at 30.5 GB/s CPU vs 12.6 GB/s PCIe gather (2.42x -> hybrid). No FP8 checkpoint fits next to the NVFP4 test model, so no end-to-end FP8 serve; the rebuilt extension leaves Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 unchanged (same answers, ~7960 prefill / ~140 decode tok/s).

36.title: feat(cpu-moe): block-FP8 expert GEMV (W8A16) for the cpu/hybrid backends
36.reason: Merged as part of #399 (its 4a04c9b), which adds the padded-scale-stride fix this PR needs for real Qwen3.x FP8 banks, an avx512f tier and stronger tests. This PR's second commit (19e9382, force each ISA tier in the test) only touches the test file that #399 rewrites with the same tier forcing.

595.title: feat(server): add ft info and a pre-load memory preflight
595.reason: Our own PR, opened from feat/ft-info (ft info + pre-load preflight, adapted to upstream main). The feature is on next since 6890aeb; the branch leaves out the parts that need upstream #562, #574, #354/#408 (follow-up PRs once those merge).

390.title: fix(models): better support for mixed-precision compressed-tensors NVFP4
390.reason: Mixed-precision compressed-tensors NVFP4 for qwen3_5_moe (FP8 attention/shared expert + NVFP4 experts, llm-compressor weight_packed / weight_global_scale names, reciprocal global scale). Superseded by #438 (0ffd5c8, every checkpoint layout through the QuantConfig): next's tests cover these exact layouts (unsloth NVFP4-Fast mixed precision, Ornith mixed-NVFP4-FP8, ct_tensor_fp8_moe), RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 serves correctly, and the PR predates the refactor (conflicts in all 5 files).

380.title: ci(container): настроить сборку образа
380.reason: Containerfile + a GitHub workflow that builds a CUDA image (publishing only in upstream's repo) and docs for `docker run`. Publishing images is upstream infrastructure this fork does not need (in the fork it would only build, up to 45 min per main push). Also, as written the documented command cannot be reached: ft serve binds 127.0.0.1 by default, so the container needs `--host 0.0.0.0`.

368.title: feat(gguf): implement Q8_0 dequantization
368.reason: Adds a torch Q8_0 dequant. Superseded by #494 (eee1723), which routes Q8_0 and every other GGML type through the gguf package's reference dequantizer; next's dequantize(Q8_0) matches the PR's formula bit for bit. The PR's test only fails on next because it imports the name dequant_q8_0.

359.title: fix(gemma4): support dense Gemma-4 GGUF checkpoints
359.reason: Lets a dense Gemma-4 GGUF parse (expert fields default to 0, moe_enabled from them). Not enough on its own, checked with google/gemma-4-12B-it-qat-q4_0-gguf: the native-quant layer swap was gated on the Q4_0 expert format (dense -> built bf16, KeyError on the packed weights) and the weight iterator asserted the offload contract without experts. Fixups: merge conflict with #494's quant layout resolved (experts laid out only when present), GGUF recognised by its tensor layout, offload assertion only for MoE. On the RTX 4090: loads, 158.7k KV tokens (preflight forecast 155.7k), correct answers, ~95 tok/s decode, ~1090 tok/s prefill; the real-GGUF rope test passes.

346.title: fix(server): stop gemma4 tool-call markers leaking into content
346.reason: Gemma4Detector surfaced partial or malformed <|tool_call markers as content; a scrub_markup hook now strips them on the one-shot paths and the end-of-stream drain (other detectors unchanged). Fixup: the scrub cut everything after the first marker, so the answer after a closed but unparseable block was lost (the PR's own example returned an empty message); a closed block is now dropped whole and only an unclosed opener ends the content. Note: streaming still turns such a block into a tool call and drops the text after it (pre-existing on next, not changed here).

341.title: feat(bench): add reproducible serving performance harness
341.reason: Client-wall serving benchmark (calibrated prompt sizes, TTFT/decode/total, prefix-cache cases, cache geometry) for a running server. Fixups: send --api-key (default $FREETOKEN_API_KEY) as a bearer header, since next's --api-key (#305) answers 401 otherwise; and the server omits prompt_tokens_details for a zero hit, so every fresh prompt read as 'no cache report' and the fresh-prefill rate was always n/a - the harness now probes whether reporting is on and counts an absent object as a miss. Live on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 (RTX 4090): 401 without key, ~150 tok/s decode, fresh prefill 1325 tok/s at 1k / 5238 tok/s at 4k, prefix hits detected (4032/4096).

340.title: fix(engine): reserve the pool's dummy page in the --moe-cache-auto KV floor
340.reason: Every KV pool keeps page 0 as a dummy, but the --moe-cache-auto plan did not count it, so it could hand that page's bytes to expert slots (OOM at boot on large pages) and --kv-reserve-tokens under-delivered by one page. Conflict with next's #562 signature (attention workspace, slot limit) resolved by keeping both; the new test dropped its quant_format argument. ft info's forecast uses the same function and follows. Live: Qwen3.6 MoE with --kv-reserve-tokens 32768 got 32850 KV tokens.

339.title: fix(kernels): drop the D2H sync from the varlen GDN/KDA prefill conv
339.reason: The triton fallback of causal_conv1d_varlen read the longest request back from the device (a D2H sync per prefill, illegal under capture); build_fla_metadata now carries the host-known max. Only the fallback is affected: with sgl_kernel installed (as here) the native kernel is used, so no speed change on this machine. New capture tests pass on the RTX 4090; Qwen3.6 MoE (GDN) serves unchanged.

338.title: perf(ple): fuse the n-gram row-id hash into one Triton kernel
338.reason: Fuses Flash-Next's PLE n-gram row-id hash (39 tiny launches per layer) into one capture-safe Triton kernel; the old torch path stays as the CPU path and test oracle, FREETOKEN_PLE_FUSED_HASH=0 restores it. Kernel-vs-reference tests pass on the RTX 4090; Flash-Next itself cannot run here, so no end-to-end speed number.

327.title: Feat/native gguf llama
327.reason: Native Llama / Llama-4 GGUF support. Does not load a standard Llama GGUF: bartowski/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct Q4_0 fails with a shape/dtype assertion during weight load (tried merged onto next). Also caps every Llama GGUF's context at 8192 (min(context_length, 8192)), drops rope_freqs without passing Llama 3's rope scaling (wrong frequencies at every position), and ships no tests; the Llama-4 MoE path is unverified. Worth doing properly as its own change if Llama GGUFs are wanted.

317.title: fix(ftw): preserve auxiliary expert banks
317.reason: Serializes 'auxiliary' expert banks (a second row geometry) into a nested FTW checkpoint and loads them back. Nothing on next produces auxiliary banks: the only producer of ExpertBanks.auxiliary_sources is the still-undecided older PR #260, so this is stacked on it. Review together with #260.

316.title: fix(rocm): avoid indirect host pointers during HIP graph capture
316.reason: Under HIP graph capture the fused expert copy's device-side pointer table loses its pinned-host mappings; the copy now falls back to per-bank copies there. CUDA is untouched (torch.version.hip is None). Conflict with next's disk-tier debug print (#337) resolved by keeping both; fixup: the PR's stub lacked next's _disk_tier attribute. Tests pass on the RTX 4090 (the ROCm-only test skips); Qwen3.6 MoE unchanged (~7900 prefill / ~139 decode tok/s). ROCm itself cannot be tested here.

315.title: Fix GGUF user-defined token atomicity
315.reason: GGUF user-defined tokens (token_type 4, e.g. <think>) keep their vocab id but transformers' GGUF conversion may not register them, so encode() split them into subwords. They are now re-added as non-special atomic tokens, only when actually split, without changing vocab size. Checked on the Gemma-4 12B GGUF: its 7 user-defined tokens already encode atomically, so nothing changes there; it matters for other GGUF architectures (e.g. once qwen35moe GGUF arrives). Tests pass.

300.title: feat: Automatic KV/MoE Laddering for decode speed vs context-length trade off ( upto 33% faster decode )
300.reason: --enable-kv-ladder: start with a small KV cache and grow it at request boundaries by shrinking the GPU expert cache (runtime rebuild), so short requests keep more experts resident. Relevant to our Qwen3.6 MoE work (expert cache vs context, TTFT floor), but needs a rework on next: it reads kwargs['moe_backend'], which next renamed to moe_strategy (crashes as soon as the flag is used), conflicts in scheduler.py and docs, and ships no tests. Revisit after the queue together with the MoE work items.

298.title: Support poolside/Laguna-S-2.1-NVFP4, and fix serving from source on Windows
298.reason: Two unrelated changes: a new Laguna model family (poolside/Laguna-S-2.1-NVFP4, ~100 GB) and a Windows serving fix (ZMQ over localhost TCP where ipc:// is missing, selector event loop, fadvise/mmap guards). Neither can be run or verified here (model far beyond the RTX 4090 / 30 GB RAM, no Windows box). Not judged on its merits yet; revisit after the queue (ideally split into the two changes).

296.title: feat(qwen3_5_moe): support compressed-tensors NVFP4 experts with block-fp8 dense side
296.reason: llm-compressor exports with NVFP4 experts and a 128x128 block-FP8 dense side (kyaky / sakamakismile, issue #263). Superseded by #438 (0ffd5c8): next's qwen3_5_moe weight tests cover exactly this layout as 'ct_block_moe', named after this PR's author's export. The PR's tests target helpers of the pre-QuantConfig loader that no longer exist.

295.title: Add Docker container capability
295.reason: Dockerfile + docker-compose + docs. The image installs freetoken from PyPI (`uv pip install "freetoken[accel]"`), not from the checkout, so an image built from this fork would hold the released upstream version without any fork changes; the docs also claim GPU support from Pascal on, which the engine's kernels do not have. Host binding is right (--host 0.0.0.0, unlike #380). Container builds are not something this fork needs.

294.title: fix(qwen3_5_moe): detect shared-expert quant for modelopt mixed checkpoints
294.reason: ModelOpt MIXED_PRECISION exports with NVFP4 experts and a per-tensor FP8 shared expert (Apodex-1.1-mini-NVFP4, issue #183) crashed at weight load. Superseded by #438 (0ffd5c8): next reads every layer's scheme from the QuantConfig; checked by adding exactly this layout to next's weight tests (6e0263b, 'modelopt_mixed_fp8_shared'): the shared expert loads as native fp8 with per-part scales broadcast over its rows, no crash.

292.title: feat: support GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4
292.reason: An independent GLM-5.3-Flash implementation (own glm5_next package with hc.py / linear_attention.py, DSA kernel changes) bundled with vast.ai serverless provisioning scripts and a worker.py for its author's infrastructure. GLM-5.3-Flash support is on next through upstream's own implementation #507 (865ed79); the provisioning scripts are out of scope for this fork.

285.title: Fix/windows serving
285.reason: A 14-commit bundle: NVFP4 and sub-byte Q4_0 KV-cache quantization with --kv-cache-dtype wiring, MSVC/Windows build and daemon fixes, /health additions, a torch 2.9 allocator workaround. Its KV-quant core is superseded by #354 (fp8 KV, --kv-cache-dtype) and #408 (nvfp4 KV) on next, and a second parallel KV-quant implementation would clash with them; the MSVC build is covered by #575. Not covered: the Q4_0 KV format and some Windows daemon/pin fixes - they would need to come back as separate, focused PRs (Windows cannot be tested here).
